Change c0156. Location: 1818 Vol. I, Ch. VI; 1831 Ch. VII.

Context before (unchanged): Good God! how can that be? who could attempt to pursue him?

1818 text: It is impossible; one might as well try to overtake the winds, or confine a mountain-stream with a straw." "I do not know what you mean; but we were all very unhappy when she was discovered.

1831 text: It is impossible; one might as well try to overtake the winds, or confine a mountain-stream with a straw. I saw him too; he was free last night!" "I do not know what you mean," replied my brother, in accents of wonder, "but to us the discovery we have made completes our misery.

Diff: It is impossible; one might as well try to overtake the winds, or confine a mountain-stream with a straw. {+I saw him too; he was free last night!+} " " I do not know what you mean [-;-] {+, " replied my brother, in accents of wonder, "+} but {+to us the discovery+} we [-were all very unhappy when she was discovered-] {+have made completes our misery+} .

Context after (unchanged): No one would believe it at first; and even now Elizabeth will not be convinced, notwithstanding all the evidence.

result.rationale: Adds Victor's dialogue 'I saw him too; he was free last night!' and rewrites Clerval/Ernest's reply, ascribing it to 'my brother' with 'accents of wonder'. The creature's freedom and Victor's active sighting heighten his guilt and sense of pursuit, changing how the scene reads.
